title: Plugin structure matches its extension surface
requirement: Use the documented layout for the actual plugin surface. Native general Python plugins need plugin.yaml and a registration entrypoint; specialized, Desktop, dashboard and portable surfaces have their own contracts. Manifest, schema, handler and registration are roles, not a requirement to copy calculator module filenames.
source_quote: - **Missing `__init__.py`:** Native packages need both `plugin.yaml` and `__init__.py` with a `register(ctx)` function. Portable packages do not import Python and do not require `__init__.py`.

title: Native Python entrypoint and callable registration
requirement: For a general native Python plugin, expose a callable register(ctx) from the package entrypoint and wire the real implementations through it. Re-exports and alternate module organization are allowed; dynamic or specialized wiring needs actual loader evidence.
source_quote: Create `__init__.py` — this wires schemas to handlers:

title: Tool schemas describe the callable interface
requirement: When tools are registered, provide meaningful descriptions and parameter schemas matching the actual handlers. Resolve static schema literals where possible; dynamic schemas require review. Schemas need not live in schemas.py.
source_quote: **Why schemas matter:** The `description` field is how the LLM decides when to use your tool. Be specific about what it does and when to use it. The `parameters` define what arguments the LLM passes.

title: Tool handlers honor the result and error contract
requirement: When tools are registered, handlers receive an argument mapping and return JSON strings on success and errors without leaking uncaught exceptions. Accepting **kwargs is forward-compatible; the guide explicitly permits handlers that name only the context they accept. Handlers need not live in tools.py.
source_quote: 2. **Return:** Always a JSON string. Success and errors alike.

title: Manifest declarations match registration
requirement: List registered tools and hooks in the native manifest and match declarations to actual behavior. Declare privileged capabilities when used and respect consent. Static names are observations, not a replacement for the official capability probe.
source_quote: List every tool your `register()` registers in `provides_tools`. The field does **not** decide whether a user-installed plugin's tools load: once the plugin is enabled, everything `register()` registers is available, declared or not. What it does drive:

title: Documented public extension surfaces only
requirement: Extend Hermes through its documented public APIs rather than runtime core replacement, private tables or application-markup workarounds. Verify surface-specific SDK requirements and unavailable-capability behavior against the guide for that surface.
source_quote: The contract covers documented surfaces only. Replacing or wrapping core

title: Profile-owned settings, state and durable storage
requirement: If settings or persistent/runtime state are used, keep user settings in the plugin namespace and runtime state in profile-scoped plugin state/data APIs, not the installed source tree or global/cross-profile configuration. Per-conversation state should use stable conversation identity where applicable.
source_quote: Never write runtime state into your plugin directory: that's the install

title: Bundled files and skills are wired correctly
requirement: If data files or skills are shipped, resolve them relative to the installed package and register bundled skills through the supported API. Verify referenced files and skill metadata without following out-of-tree paths. Data files, skills and hooks are optional, not mandatory calculator scaffolding.
source_quote: Plugins can ship skill files that the agent loads via `skill_view("plugin:skill")`. Register them in your `__init__.py`:

title: Dependencies and environment configuration are declared
requirement: Declare required Python dependencies in plugin.yaml or pyproject.toml and required environment/configuration inputs through documented declarations. Follow dependency policy and profile-safe secret routes; never read credential stores directly. No dependencies or credentials are required for a plugin that does not use them.
source_quote: - **Declare Python dependencies:** list them under `python_dependencies` in `plugin.yaml`, or in a `pyproject.toml` next to it. See [Python dependencies](#python-dependencies).

title: Optional hooks and availability use supported contracts
requirement: If hooks, lifecycle callbacks or conditional availability are used, verify hook names, callback signatures/payloads and graceful unavailable behavior. Accept additive context where appropriate; absence of optional hooks is not a failure.

title: Native commands bind session paths and context correctly
requirement: If native slash/tool commands accept filesystem paths or session context, bind to the invoking session through documented helpers rather than process-global cwd/environment, or explicitly refuse relative inputs. Do not change the shared gateway cwd to implement this. Standalone CLI cwd semantics are separate.
source_quote: - Take the session's working directory from `agent.runtime_cwd.resolve_agent_cwd()`, not `os.getcwd()`, which is the gateway's own directory. Resolve relative paths against it.

title: Discovery and actual behavior are tested
requirement: Obtain source-bound evidence that the supported loader discovers/registers the plugin and its real behavior works. Review Doctor/validator output and tests on the claimed platforms; static source shape does not prove runtime functionality. Execute trusted candidates only with operator authorization; this requirement never triggers installation automatically.

title: Human-merged gate
requirement: Entries are added *only* via a PR to the `hermes-agent` repository, reviewed and merged by a maintainer. There is no self-serve registry, no automated ingestion.

title: Exact SHA pins are mandatory
requirement: Every entry pins a full 40-character commit SHA. Branches, tags, and short SHAs are rejected by the loader. Installs clone the repository and check out exactly that commit.

title: No self-updating code
requirement: A listed plugin must not fetch and replace its own files (in-app "check for updates", signed release downloaders, remote `plugin.js` loaders). The exact SHA pin *is* the trust model; a self-updater lets an installed copy move to a commit nobody reviewed. Updates reach users only through a SHA-bump PR here plus `hermes plugins update <name>`. Keep the updater in the standalone distribution if you want one; strip it from the catalog build.

title: SHA bumps are new PRs
requirement: Updating an entry's pin is a new PR whose diff (old SHA → new SHA) is re-reviewed like any other change — reviewers are expected to look at the upstream commit range being adopted.

title: Owner-or-major-contributor submissions, or a maintainer-curated sweep
requirement: An entry may be submitted by the plugin repository's owner or a major contributor to it; drive-by submissions of third-party repos are declined. Hermes maintainers may also add entries in batches from a reviewed sweep of community plugins (every pin validated and scanned at the pinned commit, self-updater and credential-store checks run, English-first UI). Authors of swept-in entries keep control: a PR from the owner adjusting or removing their entry is accepted on request, and SHA bumps stay owner-or-maintainer PRs under rule 4.

title: Declared capabilities must match reality
requirement: The `capabilities:` block (tools, hooks, middleware, env vars) must match what the plugin actually registers at the pinned commit. Validation fails the entry otherwise — undeclared capability creep is treated as a security issue.

title: The install scanner runs at admission
requirement: `hermes plugins validate` includes the `security scan` check: `dangerous` fails the entry; `caution` findings appear as warnings in the CI log and the reviewer reads them before merging. In exchange, installs at the pinned SHA accept `caution` without a prompt (`dangerous` still blocks). Review the warnings; do not merge past them.

title: Desktop plugins stay inside the SDK surface
requirement: A `desktop/plugin.js` runs in the Desktop renderer with the app's full authority (the loader isolates errors, not capabilities), so a listed one may only use the plugin SDK: no prototype patching of renderer or browser objects (`Storage.prototype.y =`, `Object.defineProperty(...prototype`), which reviewers check by hand (the lint does not); a bundled library setting fields on classes it declares itself (three.js and the like) is fine, no `eval`/`new Function`, no `import()` of anything but `@hermes/plugin-sdk` / `react` (app bundle chunks, blob or http URLs included), no script-tag injection, no reaching into the app's internal stores or its own markup (querying `data-slot` / `data-tour` / `data-sidebar` / `data-testid` elements from `document`, or a `document.body` MutationObserver, to restyle, hide, click or rewrite core UI). `hermes plugins validate` refuses these at admission (`desktop surface` check) and warns, for the reviewer, on raw `window.hermesDesktop` bridge calls and on the app's markup selected any other way (`[data-slot]`, `[data-tree-*]` in CSS text or `closest()`); a plugin that needs a capability the SDK lacks asks for an SDK hook instead of patching around it.

title: No runtime overrides of Hermes core
requirement: A listed plugin extends Hermes only through public surfaces: hooks, middleware, provider profiles and the other `register_*` APIs, and Desktop SDK slots and routes. It must not replace, wrap or rebind core functions, methods, module attributes or private dicts in place (`AIAgent.<method> = ...`, `setattr(server, ...)`, `sys.modules[...]`, writes into a core module's tables). Two plugins patching the same seam silently break each other, and every core release can break both. `hermes plugins validate` refuses these at admission (`no core override` check), and warns (without failing) on each import of an undocumented core module and each call to a private method of a core object it is handed (`db._execute_write(...)`), by file and line. If the hook you need does not exist, open an issue describing it: we would rather add the seam than list a patch.

title: Dependency security policy is the plugin's
requirement: Hermes's 3-day `exclude-newer` release-age check covers Hermes's own dependencies only, at the time Hermes locks them; a plugin's `python_dependencies` / `pyproject.toml` install under the plugin's policy (no age check), inside Hermes's core constraints: Hermes's exact pins cannot move. Reviewers read the dependency list at the pinned SHA: bare floors (`>=X` with no upper bound) and floors on the newest release get a request for the oldest API-compatible floor plus an upper bound, and authors are strongly recommended to run their own release quarantine (`uv --exclude-newer` in their CI) — see the developer guide's *Dependency security policy*. A recent floor alone is not grounds to hold an entry.

title: Credentials come through Hermes, never from files
requirement: A plugin gets secrets only through Hermes's routes. Its declared `requires_env` and `config_schema` secrets are read with `agent.secret_scope.get_secret(NAME)`, which honours the active profile (a bare `os.environ` read can pick up another profile's key under multiplexing). A subscription sign-in (Codex / ChatGPT today) is used only through `credentialed_provider_request` with `requires_auth`, so Hermes attaches the token and the plugin never holds it. An OAuth client for a third-party API (the user's own Google Cloud client, for example) is declared under `oauth:` in `plugin.yaml`, signed in with `hermes auth add <plugin>:<id>` and used through the same helper; Hermes stores and refreshes that token too. Its `authorize_url`, `token_url` and `hosts` are `https` only, and its `hosts` belong to the API the scopes are for. A plugin never reads `.env` files, Hermes's `auth.json`, another tool's login (a vendor CLI's token file, a browser profile, a keychain) or any other credential store directly, and never refreshes, rotates or writes OAuth tokens or presents itself as another vendor's client. If Hermes has no route for a credential a plugin needs, ask for one in a Hermes issue or PR; the plugin does not work around it.

title: Approvals and unattended runs are respected
requirement: A plugin never routes around Hermes's approval system: no auto-approving, no disabling guards, and no spawning Hermes or shell children that inherit YOLO or non-interactive mode to run commands nobody approved. Anything that waits for a person (a prompt, an OAuth browser flow) fails cleanly or times out under cron, the messaging gateway and other unattended runs instead of hanging the agent.

title: Risky behaviour is disclosed
requirement: What a user would want to know before installing goes in the PR description and the plugin's README: network calls to third-party services, reads outside the plugin's own data, shell commands, long-running background processes, stored credentials. Telemetry and usage reporting are opt-in. Reviewers summarise these as disclosure lines on the entry PR; undisclosed behaviour found in review is a request for changes.

title: Compatibility metadata is truthful
requirement: `requires_hermes` is a SemVer floor (`">=0.21.5"`), never a CalVer date, and never newer than the current release. The entry's `requires_hermes` is enforced: an install by catalog name refuses on a Hermes it rejects, and `hermes plugins update` keeps an installed plugin at its current pin until Hermes is updated. Declare the same floor in `plugin.yaml` as well, because older Hermes versions enforce only that one (the loader skips the plugin when it does not match). A portable package (`plugin.json`) has no `requires_hermes` field, so the catalog entry's `requires_hermes` is its only floor: set one when the package needs a recent Hermes (a server declaration key an older release ignores). `version` matches the pinned code, and Python dependencies resolve under Hermes's core constraints (`hermes plugins validate --install-deps` is what CI runs).

title: No skins or forks of bundled plugins
requirement: A change to a bundled plugin is a PR against `hermes-agent`, not a competing listing, and vendor-lookalike skins are not listed under Nous branding.

title: One listing per plugin lineage
requirement: A fork of a listed community plugin is listed only when it is materially different from the original: a different transport or architecture, or capability the original lacks and its author declined or has not answered a PR for 30 days. Improvements to a listed plugin go upstream as a PR to its author. A fork that renames, rebrands or adds small changes is declined in favour of the original. A listed fork names its origin in its disclosure line (`Derived from <entry>`).

title: No unscannable executable payloads
requirement: Everything a reviewer and the install scanner read at the pinned commit must be source they can read. A plugin must not ship a compiled binary (a native executable or library of any OS — detected by file header, not extension: ELF, Mach-O, PE/`MZ`, WebAssembly), committed Python bytecode (`.pyc`/`.pyo`, including sourceless or hash-forged caches that run instead of the `.py` beside them), or an archive whose members are not themselves reviewable source. A plain-text source bundle (a `.tar.gz` of `.py`/`.ts`/`.md` the plugin unpacks) is read like any other source; a bundle hiding a binary is not. The scanner cannot read machine code, and a checksum committed in the same commit only proves the file was not changed after that commit, not where it came from. If a plugin genuinely needs a native component, the binary must be built by the plugin repository's own public GitHub Actions from source in that repository and carry a GitHub build attestation (`actions/attest-build-provenance`) tying it to that workflow and commit; the gate verifies the attestation against the pinned commit (`gh attestation verify --repo <owner/repo> --source-digest <pinned sha>`). A binary a user's own machine fetches at setup time is allowed only from the upstream tool's official source, pinned by checksum, and disclosed (rule 13) — never bundled and never from an unofficial mirror.

title: Password managers come from their vendor
requirement: A plugin that registers a `browser_vault` login backend (`ctx.register_login_backend`) is listed only at `tier: verified`, submitted from the password-manager vendor's own repository by that vendor, or at `tier: official` when Nous maintains it. Community-tier, fork and third-party listings of a login backend are declined. Hermes enforces the same rule when the plugin loads: a login backend is accepted only from a plugin bundled with Hermes or installed from this catalog at `verified` or `official` tier and at the reviewed pin, as recorded in Hermes's own install record (never a file inside the plugin). Local-directory, Git URL, `--ref`, `--allow-removed`, project and pip installs are refused, and no setting relaxes it.

title: Public repository
requirement: The catalog repo must be public HTTPS on GitHub or GitLab and cloneable.

title: Loadable plugin layout
requirement: plugin.yaml plus a supported Python, Desktop, portable or dashboard entrypoint at the pin; monorepos declare subdir.

title: Local catalog validation
requirement: Run hermes plugins validate PATH --install-deps at the exact pinned checkout; fix all failures and review all warnings.

title: Catalog entry and PR contents
requirement: Add one plugin-catalog/<name>.yaml; quote version; PR describes functionality, surfaces, rule-13 disclosures, and screenshots for UI.

title: Catalog CI and maintainer review
requirement: CI green and maintainer review are admission gates; checks start when a maintainer starts them, not necessarily immediately.

title: Catalog PR opened
requirement: Open a PR adding this plugin to the NousResearch/hermes-agent plugin catalog. A pending PR suffices to submit the form.

title: Public demo on X
requirement: Post a demo video on X and tag @NousResearch.

title: Demo duration and working behavior
requirement: Keep the demo strictly under 90 seconds and show the actual plugin working.

title: Submission form
requirement: Submit both the catalog PR link and X demo link through https://form.typeform.com/to/FwJLvOln .

title: Submission deadline
requirement: Announcement says 5PM EST on Nov 11th. The year is not explicit in its body; confirm the event year before comparing timestamps. EST is UTC-05:00.

title: Usefulness
requirement: Review the plugin itself for real user value. No official numerical weights or pass threshold are published.

title: Reliability
requirement: Exercise success, failure, unavailable-service and unattended behavior. Do not infer runtime reliability from source alone.

title: Polish
requirement: Review onboarding, documentation, errors, UI accessibility and coherent user experience.

title: Creativity
requirement: Review originality and fit for the Hermes plugin surfaces.

title: Beyond a prompt or skill
requirement: Judges favor capability that does more than a prompt or skill could; this is a preference, not a published eligibility ban.
